items.vignette: Cancel is grey on grey; Pause is large; confirmation relabels buttons.
items.countermove: Use keyboard to pick the correct control; capture before/after; verify in settings.
items.rationale: Visual weight and label shifts steer choice.

items.vignette: At checkout, a $4.99 “protection plan” checkbox is already ticked and sits below the fold; the visible total only reflects it once you scroll to review your order.
items.countermove: Uncheck the add-on, screenshot the cart before and after, and proceed only once the total reflects your intent.
items.rationale: Cost was added without clear disclosure — a pre-checked default hidden from the visible total.

items.vignette: To finish creating an account, one checkbox both agrees to the terms of service and opts you into marketing emails and a data-sharing partnership — there is no way to accept the terms without the rest.
items.countermove: Complete signup, then immediately open the privacy/communications settings to opt out, capturing a before/after screenshot as proof.
items.rationale: Two unrelated consents are bundled into one required action, so agreeing to the necessary thing also agrees to something you didn't choose.

items.vignette: Trying to close a discount pop-up, the only way out is a link reading “No thanks, I like paying full price” — there is no plain close button.
items.countermove: Dismiss via the browser's own close control, or click through — the guilt wording carries no legal weight either way.
items.rationale: The decline option is worded to shame you into the merchant's preferred choice rather than stating a neutral option.

items.vignette: Every time you dismiss the “Upgrade to Pro” modal, it reappears on your next click inside the app, with no permanent “don't show again” option anywhere.
items.countermove: Check account settings for a notification/upsell toggle; if none exists, note the missing opt-out as its own evidence line in your audit.
items.rationale: Repeated prompting after a clear decline is nagging — friction by repetition rather than by wording or layout.

items.vignette: A product page shows “23 people bought this in the last hour” next to a countdown timer that resets to 10:00 every time the page is refreshed.
items.countermove: Ignore the timer and counter — they carry no real deadline — and re-check price and availability on a fresh session before deciding.
items.rationale: Manufactured urgency and consensus signals are designed to rush a decision, not to convey real scarcity.

items.vignette: A bright animated “limited-time bonus” banner fills most of the screen while the actual plan-comparison table — the one showing the cheaper option — sits collapsed under a small “compare plans” link most visitors never click.
items.countermove: Look for the plan-comparison or full-details link before deciding, and screenshot the comparison table you actually chose from.
items.rationale: Attention is pulled toward flashy secondary content while the real comparison is visually buried, not mislabeled.

items.vignette: The signup flow takes one click; cancellation is phone-only, available weekdays 9–5, and the recorded message repeats “please chat with us to continue” before offering any cancel option.
items.countermove: Call once during the required hours, state a clear dated cancellation request, get a reference number, and send a same-day follow-up email documenting the call.
items.rationale: Friction is added specifically to the exit path — narrow hours and a single high-friction channel — while entry stayed effortless.

items.vignette: A “free for 30 days” trial requires a card upfront; on day 31 it silently converts to a $39.99/month plan, and the charge only ever appears as a line item on the card statement — no reminder email is sent.
items.countermove: Use a throwaway email and calendar a reminder before the trial ends, or refuse card-up-front trials entirely; if charged, your calendar note plus the original offer screenshot supports a refund request.
items.rationale: The cost and its timing are never disclosed at the moment that matters — Sneaking's cost-without-disclosure pattern, applied to renewal instead of checkout.

items.vignette: Claiming a “free” trial requires agreeing to a single checkbox that also enrolls you in a partner newsletter and waives your right to a jury trial — none of which can be unchecked separately.
items.countermove: Accept only if you're willing to opt out afterward; immediately locate the newsletter/communications setting and opt out, capturing a before/after screenshot as proof.
items.rationale: Multiple unrelated consents are locked together behind one required action — the defining trait of forced-action bundling.
